sanskrit: śrutvā senāpatiṃ prāptaṃ bharataṃ kekayādhipaḥ yudhājid gārgyasahitaṃ parāṃ prītim upāgamat
english: Hearing that Bharata, the commander of the army, had arrived together with Yudhājit of the Gārgya lineage, the lord of the Kekayas felt surpassing delight.

sanskrit: sa niryayau janaughena mahatā kekayādhipaḥ tvaramāṇo 'bhicakrāma gandharvān devarūpiṇaḥ
english: That lord of the Kekayas sallied forth with a great host of people, advancing swiftly against the Gandharvas who resembled the gods in form.

sanskrit: bharataś ca yudhājic ca sametau laghuvikramau gandharvanagaraṃ prāptau sabalau sapadānugau
english: Bharata and Yudhājit, united and swift of stride, arrived at the Gandharva city together with their armies and retinues of foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu bharataṃ prāptaṃ gandharvās te samāgatāḥ yoddhukāmā mahāvīryā vinadantaḥ samantataḥ
english: Hearing that Bharata had arrived, those Gandharvas of great valor assembled together, eager for battle, crying out on all sides.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam saptarātraṃ mahābhīmaṃ na cānyatarayor jayaḥ
english: Then a tumultuous, hair-raising battle ensued — terrible and lasting seven nights — and neither side gained victory.

sanskrit: tato rāmānujaḥ kruddhaḥ kālasyāstraṃ sudāruṇam saṃvartaṃ nāma bharato gandharveṣv abhyayojayat
english: Then Bharata, the younger brother of Rāma, enraged, discharged against the Gandharvas the dreadful weapon of Kāla called Saṃvarta.

sanskrit: te baddhāḥ kālapāśena saṃvartena vidāritāḥ kṣaṇenābhihatās tisras tatra koṭyo mahātmanā
english: Bound by the noose of Kāla and torn apart by the Saṃvarta weapon, thirty million of them were struck down in an instant by that great-souled one.

sanskrit: taṃ ghātaṃ ghorasaṃkāśaṃ na smaranti divaukasaḥ nimeṣāntaramātreṇa tādṛśānāṃ mahātmanām
english: That slaughter, terrible to behold — such a deed of great-souled men accomplished in merely the twinkling of an eye — the dwellers of heaven do not recall its like.

sanskrit: hateṣu teṣu vīreṣu bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ niveśayām āsa tadā samṛddhe dve purottame takṣaṃ takṣaśilāyāṃ tu puṣkaraṃ puṣkarāvatau
english: When those warriors had been slain, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, then established two most excellent and prosperous cities: Takṣa in Takṣaśilā and Puṣkara in Puṣkarāvatī.

sanskrit: gandharvadeśo ruciro gāndhāraviṣayaś ca saḥ varṣaiḥ pañcabhir ākīrṇo viṣayair nāgarais tathā
english: That beautiful Gandharva country, the Gāndhāra territory, was filled within five years with provinces and urban settlements.

sanskrit: dhanaratnaughasaṃpūrṇo kānanair upaśobhite anyonyasaṃgharṣakṛte spardhayā guṇavistare
english: Filled with floods of wealth and jewels, adorned with groves, the two cities rivaled each other in every excellence, vying with one another to excel in virtues.

sanskrit: ubhe suruciraprakhye vyavahārair akalmaṣaiḥ udyānayānaughavṛte suvibhaktāntarāpaṇe
english: Both were renowned for their great beauty, distinguished by spotless commerce, thronged with throngs of gardens and vehicles, with marketplaces well laid out in their quarters.

sanskrit: ubhe puravare ramye vistarair upaśobhite gṛhamukhyaiḥ surucirair vimānaiḥ samavarṇibhiḥ
english: Both were splendid foremost cities, lovely and adorned with wide expanses, graced with principal mansions of great beauty and palatial structures of matching splendor.

sanskrit: śobhite śobhanīyaiś ca devāyatanavistaraiḥ niveśya pañcabhir varṣair bharato rāghavānujaḥ punar āyān mahābāhur ayodhyāṃ kaikayīsutaḥ
english: Adorned too with the splendid expanse of shrines to the gods — having settled the land in five years, Bharata the younger brother of Rāghava, the mighty-armed son of Kaikeyī, returned to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ sākṣād dharmam ivāparam rāghavaṃ bharataḥ śrīmān brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ
english: The illustrious Bharata paid homage to the great-souled Rāghava — who was like Dharma incarnate — even as Vāsava pays homage to Brahmā.

sanskrit: śaśaṃsa ca yathāvṛttaṃ gandharvavadham uttamam niveśanaṃ ca deśasya śrutvā prīto 'sya rāghavaḥ
english: And he reported in full detail the great slaughter of the Gandharvas and the settlement of the country. Hearing this, Rāghava was well pleased with him.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā harṣam āpede rāghavo bhrātṛbhiḥ saha vākyaṃ cādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ bhrātṝn provāca rāghavaḥ
english: Hearing that, Rāghava was filled with joy together with his brothers, and Rāghava spoke to his brothers words that were wonderful to behold.

sanskrit: imau kumārau saumitre tava dharmaviśāradau aṅgadaś candraketuś ca rājyārhau dṛḍhadhanvinau
english: "O Saumitri, these two princes of yours, Aṅgada and Candraketu, accomplished in dharma and firm-bowed, are worthy of kingdoms."

sanskrit: imau rājye 'bhiṣekṣyāmi deśaḥ sādhu vidhīyatām ramaṇīyo hy asaṃbādho rametāṃ yatra dhanvinau
english: "I shall consecrate these two to kingdoms — let a suitable territory be arranged — one that is pleasant and uncrowded, where the two archers may dwell in happiness."

sanskrit: na rājñāṃ yatra pīdā syān nāśramāṇāṃ vināśanam sa deśo dṛśyatāṃ saumya nāparādhyāmahe yathā
english: "A territory should be found, dear one, where there would be no injury to kings and no destruction of hermitages — so that we commit no offense."

sanskrit: tathoktavati rāme tu bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha ayaṃ kārāpatho deśaḥ suramaṇyo nirāmayaḥ
english: When Rāma had spoken thus, Bharata replied: "This territory along the Kārāpatha road is exceedingly beautiful and free from affliction."

sanskrit: niveśyatāṃ tatra puram aṅgadasya mahātmanaḥ candraketoś ca ruciraṃ candrakāntaṃ nirāmayam
english: "Let a city be established there for the great-souled Aṅgada, and likewise a beautiful, wholesome city called Candrakānta for Candraketu."

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ bharatenoktaṃ pratijagrāha rāghavaḥ taṃ ca kṛtā vaśe deśam aṅgadasya nyaveśayat
english: Rāghava accepted the words spoken by Bharata, and having brought that territory under control, he settled it for Aṅgada.

sanskrit: aṅgadīyā purī ramyā aṅgadasya niveśitā ramaṇīyā suguptā ca rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: The lovely city known as Āṅgadīyā was founded for Aṅgada — beautiful and well-protected — by Rāma of tireless deeds.

sanskrit: candraketus tu mallasya mallabhūmyāṃ niveśitā candrakānteti vikhyātā divyā svargapurī yathā
english: And Candraketu was settled in the wrestling-ground of Malla, in the Malla country — the city famed as Candrakānta, divine like a city of heaven.

sanskrit: tato rāmaḥ parāṃ prītiṃ bharato lakṣmaṇas tathā yayur yudhi durādharṣā abhiṣekaṃ ca cakrire
english: Then Rāma, Bharata, and Lakṣmaṇa — those invincible ones in battle — were filled with great joy and performed the consecration rites.

sanskrit: abhiṣicya kumārau dvau prasthāpya sabalānugau aṅgadaṃ paścimā bhūmiṃ candraketum udaṅmukham
english: Having consecrated the two princes and dispatched them with their armies and retinues — Aṅgada toward the western land and Candraketu toward the north —

sanskrit: aṅgadaṃ cāpi saumitrir lakṣmaṇo 'nujagāma ha candraketos tu bharataḥ pārṣṇigrāho babhūva ha
english: Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, followed after Aṅgada, while Bharata became the rear-guard for Candraketu.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇas tv aṅgadīyāyāṃ saṃvatsaram athoṣitaḥ putre sthite durādharṣe ayodhyāṃ punar āgamat
english: Lakṣmaṇa dwelt in Āṅgadīyā for a full year; once that invincible prince was established, he returned again to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: bharato 'pi tathaivoṣya saṃvatsaram athādhikam ayodhyāṃ punar agamya rāmapādāv upāgamat
english: Bharata likewise dwelt there for a year and more, and then returning to Ayodhyā, he came to the feet of Rāma.

sanskrit: ubhau saumitribharatau rāmapādāv anuvratau kālaṃ gatam api snehān na jajñāte 'tidhārmikau
english: Both Saumitri and Bharata, devoted to the feet of Rāma and supremely righteous, did not notice time passing, so great was their love.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi daśateṣāṃ yayus tadā dharme prayatamānānāṃ paurakāryeṣu nityadā
english: Thus ten thousand years passed for them as they strove constantly in dharma and in the affairs of the city every day.

sanskrit: vihṛtya lākaṃ paripūrṇamānasāḥ śriyā vṛtā dharmapathe pare sthitāḥ trayaḥ samiddhā iva dīptatejasā hutāgnayaḥ sādhu mahādhvare trayaḥ
english: Having enjoyed the world with minds fully content and encompassed by glory, those three stood firm upon the highest path of dharma — like three blazing sacrificial fires of brilliant splendor kindled well at a great sacrifice.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya rāme dharmapathe sthite kālas tāpasarūpeṇa rājadvāram upāgamat
english: Then, after some time had passed, while Rāma stood firm upon the path of dharma, Kāla — Time personified — came to the royal gate in the form of an ascetic.

sanskrit: so 'bravīl lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyaṃ dhṛtimantaṃ yaśasvinam māṃ nivedaya rāmāya saṃprāptaṃ kāryagauravāt
english: He spoke to the steadfast and illustrious Lakṣmaṇa: "Announce me to Rāma — I have come on a matter of great importance."

sanskrit: dūto hy atibalasyāhaṃ maharṣer amitaujasaḥ rāmaṃ didṛkṣur āyātaḥ kāryeṇa hi mahābala
english: "For I am the messenger of a most powerful great seer of immeasurable might. O mighty one, I have come desiring to see Rāma on a matter of urgency."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saumitris tvarayānvitaḥ nyavedayata rāmāya tāpasasya vivakṣitam
english: Hearing those words, Saumitri hastened and reported to Rāma what the ascetic wished to say.

sanskrit: jayasva rājan dharmeṇa ubhau lokau mahādyute dūtas tvāṃ draṣṭum āyātas tapasvī bhāskaraprabhaḥ
english: "Be victorious by dharma in both worlds, O king of great splendor. An ascetic bright as the sun has come as a messenger wishing to see you."

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ lakṣmaṇenoktaṃ śrutvā rāma uvāca ha praveśyatāṃ munis tāta mahaujās tasya vākyadhṛk
english: Hearing the words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma said: "Dear one, let the sage of great power, the bearer of his message, be admitted."

sanskrit: saumitris tu tathety uktvā prāveśayata taṃ munim jvalantam iva tejobhiḥ pradahantam ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: Saumitri said "So be it" and ushered in that sage who blazed as if with flames and scorched with his very radiance.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya raghuśreṣṭhaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā ṛṣir madhurayā vācā vardhasvety āha rāghavam
english: Approaching the foremost of the Raghu line who blazed with his own effulgence, the seer spoke to Rāghava with sweet voice: "May you flourish!"

sanskrit: tasmai rāmo mahātejāḥ pūjām arghya purogamām dadau kuśalam avyagraṃ praṣṭuṃ caivopacakrame
english: The great-resplendent Rāma offered him worship preceded by the arghya libation, and then calmly proceeded to inquire of his welfare.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhaś ca kuśalaṃ tena rāmeṇa vadatāṃ varaḥ āsane kāñcane divye niṣasāda mahāyaśāḥ
english: Asked of his welfare by Rāma, the best among speakers and greatly renowned, he took his seat upon the divine golden throne.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato rāmaḥ svāgataṃ te mahāmune prāpayasva ca vākyāni yato dūtas tvam āgataḥ
english: Then Rāma spoke to him: "Welcome, great sage. Now deliver the words on account of which you have come as a messenger."

sanskrit: codito rājasiṃhena munir vākyam udīrayat dvandvam etat pravaktavyaṃ na ca cakṣur hataṃ vacaḥ
english: Prompted by that lion among kings, the sage began to speak: "What is to be said must be said in a private meeting — and the spoken word must not be wounded by any eye."

sanskrit: yaḥ śṛṇoti nirīkṣed vā sa vadhyas tava rāghava bhaved vai munimukhyasya vacanaṃ yady avekṣase
english: "Whoever listens or looks upon this, O Rāghava, shall be worthy of death — if, that is, you value the word of this foremost of sages."

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratijñāya rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt dvāri tiṣṭha mahābāho pratihāraṃ visarjaya
english: Having pledged "So be it," Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa: "O mighty-armed one, stand at the door and dismiss the door-keeper."

sanskrit: sa me vadhyaḥ khalu bhavet kathāṃ dvandvasamīritām ṛṣer mama ca saumitre paśyed vā śṛṇuyā ca yaḥ
english: "For he shall truly deserve death, O Saumitri, who sees or hears this private discourse between the sage and me."

sanskrit: tato nikṣipya kākutstho lakṣmaṇaṃ dvārasaṃgrahe tam uvāca muniṃ vākyaṃ kathayasveti rāghavaḥ
english: Then, having stationed Lakṣmaṇa, the scion of Kākutstha, at the keeping of the door, Rāghava said to the sage: "Speak."

sanskrit: yat te manīṣitaṃ vākyaṃ yena vāsi samāhitaḥ kathayasva viśaṅkas tvaṃ mamāpi hṛdi vartate
english: "Whatever words are in your mind, on account of which you have come with such focused resolve — speak them without hesitation; they dwell in my heart as well."
